subject: TRIM function
notes: cite.py --check 15.96.3 'Argument-1 shall be a data item of class alphabetic, alphanumeric, or national.' -> OK (r1). READ: IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified["TRIM"] = Schema("§15.96.3 r1/r2", ['s','s'], cross: MatchArgument1) — position 0 declares kind 's', and Admissible('s') = {Alphanumeric, NumericEditedDeEditing, National} (IntrinsicArgumentRules.Admissible), so Violation() rejects class numeric, boolean, index, object and pointer for argument-1. §8.5.2.1 Table 2 puts alphabetic and numeric-edited under alphanumeric, so 's' is exactly r1's three classes in this model (PicCategory folds PIC A into Alphanumeric — the CobolClass enum comment). The screen is REACHED on this bespoke path: IntrinsicBinder.BindTrim calls CheckArgumentClasses(sig, operands) at line 1010 before building the node (the generic path returns earlier), and CheckArgumentClasses walks schema.At(i). Positive coverage in both admitted rows: intrinsics_trim (PIC X(10) argument-1) and pb15_result_type_follows_argument (PIC N(8) and PIC X(8) argument-1, TRIM-N=[CDE] / TRIM-X=[CDE]). Figurative ZERO passes (candidate classes include alphanumeric — §8.3.3.6.4 GR4, PB48) and pb48_figurative_zero_intrinsic_argument pins it. NOT VERIFIED BY A FIXTURE: the rejection direction — no negative fixture feeds TRIM a class-numeric/pointer argument-1 (pb58-trim-arg2 tests r2's width, pb15-trim-national-result-to-an tests the §15.96.1 result table), so the row stays test-needed on that half; the code path was read instead. Deliberate latitude recorded, NOT scored as a defect: r1 says 'a DATA ITEM', and the implementation also admits an alphanumeric/national LITERAL argument-1. That is what §15.6 Table 21 types TRIM's argument-1 as (Alph1 or Anum1 or Nat1) and what §15.3 type 2 admits ('A data item of the class alphabetic or alphanumeric or an alphanumeric literal'), and §15.96.4's own NOTE writes TRIM("aabbcc" "c" "b") — rejecting a literal would reject the standard's own example. Editions from Annex §E.3.3 item 31 (--check OK: 'The TRIM function has been enhanced…', i.e. TRIM predates 2023) plus kb/Work R28's landed primary-source decision (WG4/J4 CD 1.2 Annex D.2 lists TRIM among the 2014 introductions); NOT derived from the IntrinsicCatalog row. REFUTED: verdict SUSTAINED — attacked on three axes and it held. (a) The load-bearing latitude citation was NOT inherited: I re-ran cite.py --check 15.3 'A data item of the class alphabetic or alphanumeric or an alphanumeric literal shall be specified' -> OK (§15.3 2), and read §15.6's own legend in the transcription ('A digit immediately following the argument type indicates the argument's position in the list of arguments') beside the Table 21 TRIM row at specs/ISO_COBOL.md — 'Alph1 or Anum1 or Nat1, Alph2 … or Anum2 … or Nat2 … or Key2 or Key2 and Alph2 …'. The literal admission is the standard's, and the Key2-then-Alph2 ordering independently corroborates the FMT-15.96.2 order finding. (b) The REJECT half was re-read rather than accepted: IntrinsicArgumentRules.CandidateClasses/ClassOf1 return a FIXED class for every operand shape that could carry a forbidden argument-1 — BoundComputedOperand{Expr: BoundIntrinsicCall} → ClassOfCategory(ic.ResultCategory), BoundComputedOperand{Expr: BoundIndexRef} → Index, bare BoundComputedOperand → Numeric, BoundFigurative 'N' (NULL) → Pointer, and ClassOfPlace keys USAGE INDEX before the category table — none is in Admissible('s'), so Violation() REPORTS instead of the candidates.Length==0 fail-open. FUNCTION TRIM(FUNCTION ABS(N)) is a compile-time §15.3 rejection, not the run-time StrArgVisitor LoudValue abort (the wrong-stage family). (c) The ALL shape was checked, since FUNCTION TRIM(ALL T) puts a TableAllPlace at position 0: ClassOfPlace reads p.Item, so argument-1's class is still screened there. The editions claim was chased to its source rather than inherited — kb/Work/R28.md's 'LANDED 2026-08-08' section names the WG4/J4 CD 1.2 (2009-08-23) Annex D.2 item 4 list verbatim, and R28's earlier body explicitly warns the 2023 PDF cannot settle a 2002 window; the adjudicator used the landed half, correctly.
